correctness.rationale: The rank-one energy Hessian has inertia transition at w=1/A; the telescoping unit-circle chord and weighted Cauchy inequality are strict at its endpoint, proving a global rather than merely local threshold. Lyapunov–Schmidt yields a supercritical quartic double well because A^3-B3>0, with global exclusivity by compactness. On the exact discrete center manifold the left cubic coefficient is h(A^3-B3)/(6Q)>0, giving the inverse-square limit by telescoping/Cesaro; transverse multipliers are stable for the explicit Laplacian step. The submitted executable checks rational edge/cubic identities, finite samples and critical iterates, but does not substitute for the proof. Limit: local dynamical rate, near-critical branch, odd cycles of length at least five.

value.rationale: A sharp, all-weight global ground-state bifurcation for every odd unicyclic graph of cycle length at least five, coupled with an exact graph-dependent critical decay coefficient, resolves an explicitly motivated frustration gap. Attached trees alter the phase-system relaxation by Q while preserving the threshold, a structural separation of equilibrium and kinetic graph effects. This is an infinite-family theorem, not finite code output or routine parameter substitution.
